newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen rebounding, weak won burdensome.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen rebounding, weak won burdensome.

text.p: Seoul Stocks are expected to rebound mildly on Tuesday after falling over the past week, but the weakening won and rising interest rates would weigh on the market, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed 1.12 points lower at 747.29 on Monday.
"A rebound is likely today after a week-long slide," said Na Min-ho of Daishin Securities.
"But deteriorating conditions in the capital markets, shown in the rising interest rates and the weakening won, remain burdensome," said Lee Moo-il of LG Securities.
The won ended Monday at 898.80 after opening at 895.00, and yields on three-year corporate bonds, South Korea's benchmark interest rate closed at 12.25 percent, up from 12.20 percent on Saturday.
Brokers said falling customer deposits with securities houses would also keep many investors on the sidelines.
Such deposits were now estimated at 3.08 trillion won, compared with a yearly high of 3.6 trillion in mid-June.
